Under the hypotheses of Lemma 6.6, if the solution is unscathed on $P(p,T_0,A\hat h,T_1-T_0)$, then the pointed region is, after parabolic rescaling by $\hat h$, $A^{-1}$-close to a pointed subset of a standard solution on $U_0\times [0,(T_1-T_0)\hat h^{-2}]$.
Proof

↗ def:kl-priori-assumptions-canonical-neighborhood-assumption ↗ lem:kl-blow-up-time-standard-solution-standard-solutions-lemma ↗ lem:kl-length-distortion-estimates-distance-distortion-lemma ↗ lem:kl-standard-solutions-existence-kappa-solutions ↗ lem:kl-surgery-pinching-condition-existence-standard-solutions \sketch Assume a counterexample sequence with surgery parameters tending to zero. Rescaled pointed compactness gives a standard-solution limit on a maximal interval; curvature and length distortion extend the convergence to the full interval $[0,T_2]$, contradicting the assumed failure of closeness.

□
